grading: Correct requires every requested material part, no contradictory caveat, no unsupported guess; partial for unresolved/omitted part without contradiction; incorrect for material source contradiction. Grade each answer independently.
selection_context: Evaluator read source and baseline summary before selecting questions.

answers.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.

Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.

Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.

Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.

Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.

Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.

Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.

Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.

Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.

Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.

Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.

May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.

Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.

Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.

Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.

Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.

Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.

Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.

Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.

Home base is not territory for any game effect; cannot normally move back in, build/deploy there. Starts and forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare explicit movement exception. Two unrepresented bases are expansion placeholders/inactive.
answers.novelty: Home-base status and default prohibitions beyond setup.

answers.expected_answer: Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village workers. Lake/Factory nothing. Workers not resources. Resource supply unlimited; use multipliers as necessary, no territory token/unit limit.
answers.novelty: Production terrain mapping and unlimited supply.

answers.expected_answer: All units may pick/drop any resources; mechs also own workers, never character. Speed adds one territory for character/mechs, including before/after tunnel jump which costs one move; may pick/drop mid-move. Entering enemy unit ends movement/cannot move again turn; character encounter also stops.
answers.novelty: Speed transport and tunnel interaction.

answers.expected_answer: Yes any unit may enter structure-only territory and controls it; no combat from structure alone. All printed tunnel territories adjacent for Move by any unit; enemy Mine not a public tunnel.
answers.novelty: Structure-only capture branch versus worker/plastic occupation.

answers.expected_answer: Never partial payment; full cost required. Take a dead turn choosing another section with no actions, still moving token.
answers.novelty: No-affordable-action dead-turn branch.

answers.expected_answer: Armory adds 1 power when owner takes Trade, Monument adds 1 popularity when owner takes Bolster. Uncovered benefits apply future respective top actions, regardless territory control; opponent never gains them. Factory similar actions excluded.
answers.novelty: Remaining building benefits and persistence.

answers.expected_answer: Riverwalk only character/mechs: Saxony and Nordic forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic faction Swim workers only across rivers to any land terrain, never lakes; no mech/character benefit.
answers.novelty: Distinct terrain crossing and Swim exception.

answers.expected_answer: Underpass controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mechs. Township controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mechs. Not workers; required ability unlocked via deploy.
answers.novelty: Faction shortcut networks and qualifying control.

answers.expected_answer: Disarm before combat on printed tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power once per combat, not per unit. Artillery before any combat may pay 1 power to make opponent lose 2, once per combat. Track losses; attacker ability before defender.
answers.novelty: Distinct combat ability triggers and payment.

answers.expected_answer: Three cards: one per mech plus one total for at least one worker. Need character/mech; workers alone cannot fight. Ability unlocked.
answers.novelty: Worker presence extra-card exception.

answers.expected_answer: From territory or home base to own home base or any inactive faction home base regardless distance, including inactive expansion bases. Not active opponent home base; workers do not gain ability.
answers.novelty: Home-base movement exception and inactive destination.

answers.expected_answer: Scout before combat randomly steals one opponent combat card to hand, once per combat not per unit. Coercion once per turn spends one combat card as any one resource regardless card value; card not worth end-game coins.
answers.novelty: Distinct hand theft and resource substitution rules.

answers.expected_answer: Both character/mechs to/from lakes, workers only via mech; cannot leave workers/resources behind when carrier leaves; worker cannot leave without mech. Nordic may retreat character/mechs onto adjacent lake (or home), carrying workers; Polania may move lake to any lake, no such special retreat. Both cannot build/deploy lake, can fight another lake-capable faction there.
answers.novelty: Lake movement/retreat exceptions and mandatory cargo.

answers.expected_answer: Prevents popularity loss for workers forced to retreat after winning combat as aggressor on own turn. Does not apply to driving out undefended workers without combat; normal one popularity each then.
answers.novelty: Combat-only popularity exception.

answers.expected_answer: Draw just one card; may choose up to two different options in either order; may use first benefit to pay second cost.
answers.novelty: Encounter option/sequence faction exception.

answers.expected_answer: No character movement again that turn; Factory Move obeys stop rules. Encounter after entire Move and all combats; character must remain there. Bottom Factory Move still triggers normal encounter.
answers.novelty: Factory movement encounter timing exception.

answers.expected_answer: Coin holdings not hidden but need not reveal total value; combat card count public, contents secret; may conceal whether cards used in combat until reveal. Objectives secret until revealed.
answers.novelty: Information visibility procedural rule.

answers.expected_answer: Only tangible exchange coins (tournament exception no coin trades for deals/alliances); informal agreements unenforceable. Cannot cancel already initiated combat by negotiation; must fight after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.
answers.novelty: Negotiation limits and mandatory combat.

answers.expected_answer: 0-6: stars3/territories2/pairs1;7-12:4/3/2;13-18:5/4/3. Lakes count if controlled, home bases never. Factory three total. Sum controlled resources across board and score floor(total/2), no leftover single; workers not resources.
answers.novelty: All scoring tier boundaries and territory/resource branches.

answers.expected_answer: Count each qualifying adjacent feature once across structures. Rivers do not break adjacency; removed encounter tokens still count printed encounter. Mine not tunnel for tile. Adjacent tunnels count1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6=$9; lakes/encounters1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6-7=$9; zero=$0.
answers.novelty: Three adjacency structure-tile rules and diagram payouts.

answers.expected_answer: On printed tunnels not Mine:1=$2,2=$4,3-4=$6. Longest continuous straight line only, rivers do not break:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Farms+tundras combined number with structures:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Zero=$0. Bonus regardless territory control.
answers.novelty: Remaining three structure-tile qualification/payout branches.

answers.expected_answer: Yes one popularity per forced-retreat worker even carried on lake; retreat with mech to home base by default (Nordic Seaworthy permits adjacent-lake retreat). Polania unlocked Camaraderie exception after combat.
answers.novelty: Lake carried-worker popularity branch.

answers.expected_answer: Star itself permanent, popularity may fall and final payout uses current tier. Other factions may also place same goal; no blocking.
answers.novelty: Irreversible star versus mutable scoring metric.

answers.expected_answer: Randomly shuffle the Faction Mats and Player Mats and deal one of each to each player. Players sit near their faction home bases, with the clockwise order from the top Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, using the factions in the game. Recruit ongoing bonuses respond to the player and their immediate left/right neighbors, so those neighbors follow the seating arrangement.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONGOING BONUS and PLAYER ORDER
answers.novelty: Distinct setup selection and required relative seating procedure. Q01 asks Factory/encounter/structure setup and start player; Q02 asks piece placement and starting values; Q12 assumes already established left/right neighbors. None elicits or keys mat assignment or seating.

answers.expected_answer: A river lies on the border between two land territories. A lake comprises an entire territory hex and extends from that hex to any adjacent shoreline. A unit with the appropriate lake-movement ability can move onto it from any of the surrounding territories shown by that shoreline; crossing permission for a river alone does not grant entry to lakes.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES; RIVER; LAKE; illustrated example
answers.novelty: Distinct source-defined map adjacency rule, rather than another example of the already tested faction ability permissions. Q27/Q33 distinguish abilities and destinations but do not define the geographic boundary or surrounding-shoreline adjacency used to apply those abilities.

answers.expected_answer: The encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud, then read through its costs and benefits and choose an option. The rules do not require reading every option aloud.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 24, ENCOUNTERS: Show the art to the other players and read the thematic text (the text in all caps) out loud.
Rulebook PDF p. 24, concluding DESIGNER'S NOTE: encounter cards are shown to all players when drawn.
answers.novelty: Distinct mandatory public-information procedure. Q15 does not ask encounter visibility or presentation, Q37 asks only coins/combat cards/objectives, and no expected answer in Q01-Q45 states this procedure. The tested outcome is whether a player may hide a drawn encounter from the table, not a changed quantity, cosmetic rewording, or mechanical combination.

answers.expected_answer: There is no per-territory limit on same-faction units or resource tokens. This does not remove the separate one-structure-per-territory restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p11 NO LIMIT: no limit to same-faction units on a territory
Rulebook PDF p13 NO LIMIT: any number of resource tokens or workers can be on a territory
answers.novelty: Distinct explicit occupancy rule. Unlimited carrying, unlimited resource supply, and production output do not establish unlimited placement in one territory. Q22 key supplies this as extra information, but Q22 wording never requests occupancy.

answers.expected_answer: The next clockwise player may begin when the current player starts or is finalizing a bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. The ordinary alternative is to start after the current turn is complete. This overlap does not reverse the stated recruit-bonus priority or the immediate game-end rule.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10 GAMEPLAY, paragraph beginning After you have completed your turn
Rulebook PDF p31 TURNS AND PLAYER MATS
answers.novelty: Distinct explicit permission governing the start of the next turn, absent from all 46 questions and keys. It is not another recruit-priority example or a recombination of action effects.

answers.expected_answer: No. Each action may be taken only once during the turn; paying the full cost again does not permit repeating it.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10 GAMEPLAY, once-per-action restriction
answers.novelty: Distinct restriction on repetitions within a turn. Q03 section repetition concerns action-token selection on successive turns, a different rule. The extra once-per-action phrase in its key is not requested by that wording.

answers.expected_answer: You may choose to gain $1 instead of moving units. Moving and gaining the listed coins are alternative choices.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p11 MOVE: move units OR GAIN COIN(S)
answers.novelty: Previously unelicited top-row action alternative, rather than a changed amount or another movement example. Q05 key includes the alternative but Q05 only asks movement and transportation.

answers.expected_answer: No. Once on the board, a worker never returns to the Player Mat. A forced retreat puts it on the home base, not back on its Produce rectangle.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p13 WORKERS ARE PERMANENT
Rulebook PDF p23 LOSER: retreat all units to home base
answers.novelty: Distinct permanent worker-removal restriction and its cost consequence. Q09 discusses newly uncovered costs and Q14 asks a specific combat retreat destination, but neither asks whether the player can later return workers to the mat. The retreat reference illustrates the same permanence rule; it does not introduce a new combined mechanic.

answers.expected_answer: Yes. Neither power nor popularity has a minimum requirement for initiating combat. You can select zero power on the dial.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p22 NO REQUIREMENTS and SELECT POWER
answers.novelty: Explicit eligibility branch. Q13 asks what may be spent, and Q06 asks expelling undefended workers at zero popularity; neither directly tests whether combat itself can be initiated without these commodities.

answers.expected_answer: Yes. The limit restricts further combat stars, not participation or winning. It may continue fighting but gains no additional combat-victory stars.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p23 LIMITED STARS AND GAME END
answers.novelty: Explicit permission after an achievement cap. Q14 covers immediate combat aftermath and Q18 asks which achievements award stars; neither requires answering whether later combat remains legal.

answers.expected_answer: You must choose one option and pay any listed cost. An option whose cost you cannot pay is unavailable. You may take as much or as little of the chosen option benefit as you want.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p24 REQUIRED COST AND OPTIONAL BENEFIT
answers.novelty: Explicit encounter-choice branches: mandatory selection, affordability and optional benefit. Existing questions ask timing, location, isolation, Polania extra options or public presentation. The three clauses are the source-defined branches of one choice procedure, not a scenario combining separate mechanics.

answers.expected_answer: They select dial power simultaneously and secretly, then reveal both Power Dials and any selected combat cards simultaneously. Attacker-first resolution of combat mech abilities does not make the power selection or reveal sequential.
answers.novelty: Distinct simultaneous commitment/reveal timing procedure. Q13 asks secret spending and ability order without asking selection/reveal timing; Q37 asks visibility of information. Its correct extra key fact does not itself elicit this procedural timing.

answers.expected_answer: You must announce that you are taking the bottom-row action, so the players immediately to your left and right can check their Recruit Ongoing Bonuses.
answers.novelty: Distinct mandatory action-announcement procedure. Q12 key includes it as extra detail, but its question only asks recruitment/bonus mechanics; other visibility questions do not concern action declarations. This is not another recruit-trigger example.

answers.expected_answer: An earned star must be placed on the appropriate achievement immediately; it cannot be declined or delayed to avoid ending the game. You may instead wait to reveal a completed objective, provided you still satisfy it when you reveal it; when you reveal it, place the star.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p27 PLACING STARS: when you achieve one of these goals, you must place a star
Rulebook PDF p2 TRIUMPH TRACK: as soon as you complete a requirement
Rulebook PDF p26 OBJECTIVES: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal
answers.novelty: Distinct mandatory placement/timing restriction, with the source-defined voluntary objective-reveal exception. Existing questions ask what earns stars and what happens after placement, not whether an already earned nonobjective star can be withheld. Q17 already covers delaying objective reveal; it supplies the precise exception rather than a new mechanically combined scenario.

answers.expected_answer: No. By default, none of the three unit types may cross rivers or move onto lakes. An applicable special ability is required to override the relevant restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 5: TYPES OF UNITS: all three unit types can move around the board, not over rivers or onto lakes by default.
Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES: By default, units may not move across rivers or onto lakes; some mech abilities break the rule.
answers.novelty: This is the source's categorical default movement restriction, distinct from the scope and destinations of particular exceptions. Q27 can be fully answered by listing each faction's Riverwalk and Nordic Swim permissions; Q45 can be fully answered by defining river borders and lake shorelines. A reader could answer both while incorrectly believing other units have unrestricted water movement. The proposal asks no new numerical example or combined ability scenario.

answers.expected_answer: No. An enlisted recruit token remains on its chosen Faction Mat space permanently and cannot be moved. You cannot free an occupied one-time bonus space by relocating that token.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONE-TIME BONUS: place the recruit on any open Recruit One-Time Bonus space; the token remains there permanently and cannot be moved.
answers.novelty: This tests the explicit immobility restriction after initial placement. Q12's substantive wording asks where the recruit goes when enlisting, rather than whether it may later move; its key's word permanently is an unasked extra. The restriction has a gameplay consequence because rearrangement could reopen a one-time bonus space for reuse. It is a single source-defined placement/lifecycle restriction, analogous to the independently tested worker and structure permanence rules, not a recombination of unrelated mechanics.

answers.expected_answer: No. Only characters trigger encounters. A mech or worker entering a territory does not resolve its encounter or remove the encounter token; it remains for a character.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p.5, TYPES OF UNITS: characters can have encounters; other units have different roles.
Rulebook PDF p.24, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters will trigger an encounter. Token removal occurs when resolving the character-triggered encounter.
Rulebook PDF p.31, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters may have encounters.
answers.novelty: A categorical unit-eligibility restriction with a consequential board-state outcome. Q15 asks timing after contested entry, the losing-character branch, benefit placement and isolated costs; Q36 asks stopping and timing when a character arrives via Factory Move; Q46 asks information presentation; Q54 asks choosing options after drawing. All can be answered correctly while incorrectly allowing a mech or worker to trigger an encounter. Q16 explicitly asks who takes a Factory card, but Factory eligibility does not elicit encounter eligibility. Q05 only asks movement/carriage, Q30 combat eligibility. The additional question introduces no changed quantities, new layout, unrelated combination or reference-only procedure.
